name: What paperwork should I review before signing a kitchen remodeling contract?

mainEntity.name: What paperwork should I review before signing a kitchen remodeling contract?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before signing, obtain the proposal, plans, material specifications, allowances, exclusions, payment schedule, estimated milestones, permit responsibilities, insurance information, change-order procedure, cleanup expectations, warranty terms, and final-inspection responsibilities. Confirm the legal name of the contracting entity and the people authorized to make decisions. Context: A kitchen remodel has many separate deliverables, so verbal promises are easy to misunderstand. Key factors: - Who owns design documents and selections. - How delays and substitutions are handled. - How incomplete or corrective work is documented. Practical guidance: Review every allowance against an actual product or a realistic range, and ask what happens if a selection exceeds it. Do not sign with unresolved scope gaps or blank change-order terms. Soft positioning: Elite Remodeling & Design’s published process spans consultation, design, permitting, construction, and final inspection, so those stages should be reflected clearly in the project documents.
acceptedAnswer.description: Review the complete scope, plans, specifications, allowances, exclusions, payment schedule, milestones, permit duties, insurance, change-order rules, cleanup, warranty, and final-inspection responsibilities. Resolve blank or vague terms before signing, especially who handles selections, substitutions, delays, and concealed-condition work.
